correctness.rationale: The code/acyclic digraph bijection follows from the two possible cyclic framings. Strand closure is an arc-reversing complement involution. All valid graphs are exactly the acyclic assignments in nine independent three-state undirected-pair orbits, so the DFS search examines all 3^9 possibilities. A separately proven source/sink induction embeds each valid graph into one of 48 complement-symmetric orders; enumerating their 2^9 closed subsets reproduces all 8,383 graphs. Orbit counts 220 are obtained both from explicit group-orbit enumeration and independently by Burnside fixed points. Code lists of all 220 representatives are embedded and verified.

originality.rationale: Closest full-text results cover maximal four-letter dinucleotide circular codes, arbitrary-alphabet maxima only, or the graph/acyclicity criterion; none inspected supplies the sixteen six-symbol all-size counts or the 220 symmetry-class refinement. The strongest general structural results are premises, not recast as new. Targeted published-record and bibliographic searches found no implication that determines the new census. Historical priority remains qualified because some plausible full texts were not accessible.
residual_risks: The complete 2014 arbitrary-alphabet maximum-code article could not be read; its abstract strongly scopes it to maxima, but unindexed additional enumerations cannot be excluded.
The two author-hosted PDF page-image retrieval attempts timed out; relevant theorem and scope text were available, not a complete verified visual read.
A historical census under different terminology (self-dual signed partial orientations/type-B weak orderings) might exist outside indexed sources.

value.rationale: The first larger even complement-pair alphabet beyond the classic four-letter case admits a complete size-refined classification, not just an easily anticipated maximum. Its nine orbit-choice dimensions yield 8,383 feasible labeled codebooks and 220 mathematically distinct classes. Michel–Pirillo 2013 expressly motivates larger alphabets; the precise finite enumeration and explicit full catalog are reusable natural invariants, without suggesting unsupported biological performance.
